Statement._comment: GetHarness returns a harness's env vars and systemPrompt, and UpdateHarness rewrites its prompt on the DEFAULT endpoint every run invokes through. On Resource '*' these reached every harness in the account, including other projects' -- a logged-in console user could repoint any agent's behaviour (2026-10-28 security audit, Batch 2a). Scoped to this project's harnesses; the console only ever reads/optimises llmops_* and the handlers also require the approver group now.

Every object the console reads, and nothing else. This was GetObject+ListBucket on "*" -- every bucket in the account -- for a console that reads one bucket. The patterns are DERIVED from lambda_function.py by tests/test_console_s3_scope.py in both directions: a literal key (runs/{run_id}/manifest.json -> runs/*, the rate card's exact key) or a _scoped_key(...) prefix tuple (_PLAN_S3_PREFIXES, _INTAKE_S3_PREFIXES, _UPLOAD_S3_PREFIXES). A read the code adds without a grant fails the test, and so does a grant nothing reads. HeadObject is authorised by GetObject. The Data tab reads lakehouse/reports/* and each dataset's lakehouse/landing/*/manifest.json, NOT the rest of landing/: that is the raw generated data, PII plants included, and the tab shows only what the reports and the manifest say. Not reports/ or code/: the console reads neither.

ListBucket is a BUCKET action, so it is scoped by the s3:prefix condition, not by the resource. runs/ and customer-data/ are intake's existence checks (list_objects_v2 Prefix=key, so 'not found' does not depend on S3's 404-vs-403 choice for a missing key; measured 2026-10-15, a GetObject on a missing runs/ key still returned NoSuchKey under this scoped grant); models-mirror/ is the mirror-presence check; lakehouse/reports/ is the Data tab's dataset picker. A list with no prefix, or under any other prefix, is denied.

Intake normalization verifies a customer-named Knowledge Base (status + latest ingestion). NAMING TRAP: these are bedrock-agent API calls but IAM authorizes them under the bedrock: action prefix — same class of gotcha as budgets:ViewBudget below. The orchestrator role deliberately does NOT get these; the console checks what the agent cannot.

Shadow estimates only: accept_task writes one est-task-* row per signed plan, which the reconcile Lambda reads. PutItem and nothing else since the v1 estimator, approval queue and estimates list were removed (2026-10-12) -- the Get/Update/Query/Scan they needed, and the GSI resource, went with them. Actuals are written only by the finops agent via the driver, so the console reads them and never writes -- a dashboard that can edit reconciled cost is not an audit trail.

Read-only on billing, deliberately. ce:* and pricing:* have no resource-level ARNs so Resource must be * -- the scoping is that only Get/List/Describe verbs appear here. Budgets surfaces the existing $1000 account guardrail rather than duplicating it. budgets:ViewBudget is the action the DescribeBudgets API actually authorizes against -- the IAM action name and the API call name differ, and granting only 'budgets:DescribeBudgets' produced a live AccessDeniedException naming budgets:ViewBudget on every Cost tab load. Both are listed: ViewBudget is what is enforced, DescribeBudgets is harmless and keeps the grant readable against the call it serves.

The ONLY write the Cost tab's enforcement policy can perform, and only when its 'Stop running jobs over budget' switch is ON (default OFF): budget_sweep stops a breached run's execution of THIS state machine and its in-progress training jobs. Scoped to the two resource families the sweep attributes to the project (COST_JOB_PREFIXES); endpoints are deliberately absent -- teardown stays with the pipeline's own Teardown stage, and DeleteEndpoint is not reversible. The grant exists whether or not the switch is ON; the switch is the policy, IAM is the ceiling.

AdminListGroupsForUser is required for the approver check: GetUser returns the username and attributes but NOT group membership, and a bearer access token carries no cognito:groups claim. Without this call the separation-of-duties gate has nothing to check. RevokeToken is what makes sign-out mean something: the refresh cookie is cleared client-side regardless, but without this grant the 30-day refresh token stays valid in Cognito for its whole window, so a sign-out on a shared machine would be cosmetic. These operations accept unauthenticated callers, but boto3 signs them with this role's credentials, and a signed request IS authorized against IAM -- so the grant is required, not decorative. InitiateAuth covers both USER_PASSWORD_AUTH (login) and REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH (session restore); it is one action, not two.

Tasks tab: the console worker IS the chat host for the orchestrator consultation. Dual-ARN shape is the known gotcha: InvokeHarness on the harness ARN AND InvokeAgentRuntime on the runtime ARN, or AccessDeniedException. Scoped to the orchestrator alone — the console must not be able to drive the stage workers directly (supreme directive: stages are dispatched by the state machine).
Task conversation records; PITR-backed audit objects. Full CRUD is correct here: the console is the only writer.
Task lifecycle events land in the same stage-events table the pipeline uses (run_id = task id) so one table answers both 'what happened in this run' and 'who did what in this consultation'.

Approval-record signing. Sign is the power to mint 'a human said yes' — console only, this one key. Verify/GetPublicKey are deliberately broad in the key policy; here the console needs them to self-check and to serve the auditor endpoint.
plan.json / approval.json / transcript objects live under tasks/. Write scoped to that prefix; S3ConsoleRead covers the GetObject on tasks/*.

The customer's own dataset, uploaded by their browser through a presigned PUT this role signs (see data_upload_url). generate_presigned_url signs with THIS role's credentials and never calls AWS, so without this grant the URL is minted happily and then 403s in the browser at the end of the upload -- the grant is part of the feature, not an afterthought. Scoped to customer-data/ and NOT merged into S3TasksWrite: a bucket-wide PutObject would let a console bug overwrite run manifests and the signed approval records under runs/, which are the evidence trail for spend. The harness execution role deliberately keeps this prefix read-only (deploy/iam/harness_execution_role.json): a pipeline that can rewrite the customer's data can destroy the held-out set its own gates are judged on. The console signs writes; the pipeline only reads.
page_human during a consultation goes to the same escalations topic the pipeline uses.
